headline: Satya Nadella becomes chief executive
text: On 4 February Microsoft named Satya Nadella, head of its cloud and enterprise division and at the company since 1992, as chief executive. Bill Gates leaves the chairmanship to become a technology adviser; John Thompson becomes chairman.
imageCaption: Satya Nadella with Bill Gates and Steve Ballmer, Redmond, 4 February 2014

headline: Sony sells its Vaio PCs and spins off TVs
text: Sony announced the sale of its Vaio PC division to the investment fund Japan Industrial Partners and will turn its television business into a separate company. The TV business has lost about 7.8 billion dollars over a decade.

headline: Record deliveries and a plan for a giant battery factory
text: Tesla delivered a record 6,892 Model S in the fourth quarter, had positive free cash flow and expects deliveries to grow by more than 55% in 2014. On 26 February it announced 1.6 billion dollars of convertible bonds to help pay for a huge battery factory, the 'Gigafactory', to make cheaper batteries for a mass-market car.
source: Tesla Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2013 Shareholder Letter, 19 February 2014, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312514058778/d676319dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); Tesla 8-K exhibit of 26 February 2014 (convertible notes), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312514069704/d685452dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Tesla,_Inc. (bonds for the Gigafactory, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Tesla Model S at the Geneva motor show

headline: Swiss voters back limits on immigration
text: On 9 February Swiss voters accepted the SVP's initiative 'against mass immigration' by 50.3 percent, a margin of 19,526 votes, and a majority of cantons. It requires quotas on immigration within three years, which contradicts the free movement of people agreed with the EU in the bilateral treaties. Brussels warned that free movement is not negotiable.
imageCaption: Federal Councillor Simonetta Sommaruga, the justice minister responsible for immigration policy

headline: Russia annexes Crimea
text: After Ukraine's pro-Russian president Viktor Yanukovych fled Kiev in February, soldiers without insignia seized Crimea's parliament and key sites. A referendum under occupation on 16 March was declared a vote to join Russia, and Russia annexed the peninsula on 18 March. The United States and the EU imposed sanctions and travel bans, and Russia was suspended from the G8.
imageCaption: President Putin with Crimean leaders at the signing of the treaty on Crimea's accession, Moscow, 18 March 2014

headline: Fraud at Banamex; Citigroup fails the stress test again
text: Citigroup disclosed a $235 million after-tax loss from a fraud at Banamex, its Mexican bank, discovered in February, and cut its 2013 results. On 26 March the Federal Reserve again rejected its capital plan, this time on concerns about the quality of its risk management.
imageCaption: A former Banco Nacional de Mexico (Banamex) building, Mexico

headline: A seven-for-one split and 130 billion dollars for shareholders
text: On 23 April Apple said it will return more than 130 billion dollars to shareholders by the end of 2015, raise its share buyback to 90 billion dollars and its dividend by about 8%, and split its shares seven for one. Apple has paid a dividend again since 2012, its first since 1995.
imageCaption: Apple's headquarters at One Infinite Loop, Cupertino
imageCredit: CC BY-SA 3.0, photo: Joe Ravi (Shutterstock iStock Dreamstime)

headline: The Microsoft sale closes; Nokia is a network company
text: The sale of the phone business to Microsoft was completed in April. Nokia now consists mainly of its network equipment arm, its HERE maps and its patent licensing.
imageCaption: Stephen Elop on stage at Nokia's press event, Mobile World Congress, Barcelona, February 2014
imageCredit: CC BY 2.0, photo: Maurizio Pesce from Milan, Italia

headline: Asset swap with GlaxoSmithKline
text: Novartis announced in April that it will buy GlaxoSmithKline's cancer drug business for $16 billion and sell its vaccines business to GSK for $7.1 billion; the two also plan a joint venture in consumer health products.
imageCaption: The GlaxoSmithKline headquarters on the Great West Road, Brentford

headline: Credit Suisse pleads guilty in the US
text: On 19-20 May Credit Suisse pleaded guilty in the United States to conspiring to help American clients evade taxes, and agreed to pay about $2.6 billion in fines and restitution.

headline: Islamic State seizes Mosul and declares a caliphate
text: Fighters of the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant captured Mosul, Iraq's second city, between 4 and 10 June as Iraqi soldiers fled, and swept towards Baghdad. About half a million people fled Mosul. On 29 June the group declared a caliphate across the parts of Iraq and Syria it controls.
imageCaption: A wrecked Humvee in Mosul after the Islamic State attack, 14 June 2014
imageCredit: CC BY-SA 4.0, photo: Omar Siddeeq Yousif

headline: eBay to spin off PayPal
text: On September 30 eBay announced it will separate PayPal into an independent listed company, as the activist investor Carl Icahn demanded at the start of the year.
imageCaption: PayPal's headquarters in San Jose, California

headline: Netflix arrives in Switzerland
text: In September the American streaming service Netflix started in Switzerland, Germany, Austria, France, Belgium and Luxembourg. For a monthly fee it shows films and series over the internet, whenever the viewer wants.

headline: IBM pays to get rid of its chip factories and drops its 2015 target
text: On 20 October IBM agreed to hand its chip manufacturing business to GlobalFoundries and to pay it 1.5 billion dollars over three years, taking a 4.7 billion dollar charge. It also said it no longer expects to earn at least 20 dollars a share in 2015, a target it had promised for years. Chief executive Ginni Rometty said the results were not what IBM expected.
imageCaption: IBM's Blue Gene/Q supercomputer 'Mira' at Argonne National Laboratory
imageCredit: CC BY 2.0, photo: Argonne National Laboratory

headline: OPEC refuses to cut
text: On 27 November in Vienna, Saudi oil minister Ali al-Naimi blocked calls from poorer OPEC members to cut output, saying the market should find its own level. US crude fell about 10% by 28 November to $65.94, down from $107 in June. US crude output is about 9.3 million barrels a day, up by two thirds in four years.
imageCaption: Ali al-Naimi, Saudi Arabia's oil minister

headline: Oil slides below 70 dollars
text: US crude, about 107 dollars a barrel in late June, closed November at about 66 dollars as a glut builds: US oil production has nearly doubled since 2008 thanks to shale fracking, and Saudi Arabia argues for lower prices to squeeze high-cost shale producers rather than for OPEC cuts. For ExxonMobil, which earned more than 32 billion dollars a year in 2013, every dollar off the oil price cuts profit.
source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010s_oil_glut (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 2 February 2015 (2013 and 2014 earnings), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408815000004/f8k4q991.htm (read 2026-10-03)
